title: Fix lacking physics interpolation on `GPUParticles2D`

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #124089
- *Bugsquad edit: Partially addresses https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/92006.*

## Additional information

<!--
Provide additional information and explanation of your PR, including areas that you are uncertain of or require special attention from reviewers. For examples, please read our pull request guidelines: https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#explain-your-contributions

### Summary

Added functionality for physics interpolation against individual particles within `GPUParticles2D`. Whilst the node itself is interpolated, the transform propagated to the particles is not.

Particles using global positioning use an inverse of the global transform of the node to "undo" the local transform. Because this inverse transform is not interpolated, but the node's transform is, a very noticeable jitter is observed when physics interpolation is enabled.

This fix adds recognition of physics interpolation when configuring the particle properties.

### Motivation

Physics interpolation is very important for modern games, and it is very typical to want to attach a particle emitter to a physics body whilst also benefitting from smooth interpolation of the postion.

### Related Work

No known related work.

### Technical Overview

Taking inspiration from how `CPUParticles2D` performs this, a current and previous transform is recorded. The strategy for this in the CPU version, however, is somewhat complex and I felt I could simplify it:

- Observe reset physics interpolation messages.
- During internal processing:
  - Update the current and previous transforms if the last observed physics frame is different from the current physics frame. This captures any changes that may have happened over the course of the entire physics tick, either directly during physics_process, or from parent propagation.
  - Call the method to update the emission transform in the particle data.
    - Within this method, if physics interpolation is enabled, perform the interpolation according to the current fraction.

### Testing

I tested against the MRP in #124089, observing that the jitter is no longer present.

I also tested with `local_coords` enabled (the mode where the jitter was never actually observed within the particles) and there were no new issues introduced.

I then tested with physics interpolation disabled on the individual `GPUParticles2D` node. The jitter was re-introduced, as expected.

I tested with physics interpolation disabled at project level and no new issues were introduced - it behaves like it did before, with no jitter.

### Discussion

I don't have any reason to believe that this change has any negative impact on the engine. It fixes a bug that would be a noticeable visual improvement to applications and games that are currently exhibiting the issue.

No AI was used to implement or document this change.
